claim: FAR 52.204-25 (Nov 2021) prohibits executive agencies from procuring equipment that uses telecommunications equipment produced by Huawei or ZTE, and (for public safety, government-facility security, critical-infrastructure surveillance and national security) video surveillance and telecom equipment produced by Hytera, Hikvision or Dahua, or their subsidiaries/affiliates; Section 889(a)(1)(A) applies from 2019-08-13 and 889(a)(1)(B) (contracting with an entity that uses such equipment) from 2020-08-13.

FAR 25.003 (FAC 2026-01, effective 2026-03-13): 'Designated country' for the Trade Agreements Act means WTO GPA countries (the list includes Taiwan as the Separate Customs Territory), FTA countries (including Mexico and Singapore), least-developed and Caribbean Basin countries; China is not on the list.

14 CFR 89.105 (eCFR as of 2026-11-09): after 2023-09-16 no person may operate an unmanned aircraft in US airspace unless it is a standard remote-ID aircraft (89.110) or carries an FAA-accepted remote-ID broadcast module or flies inside an FAA-recognized identification area (89.115); producers attest compliance with an FAA-accepted declaration of compliance (89.1).

47 CFR 15.212 (eCFR as of 2026-11-09): a modular transmitter with its own grant must carry its FCC ID label or e-label; if the module's label is not visible when installed, the host product must carry an exterior label referring to the enclosed module (the pre-certified-module route used when a host integrates a radio).

EDPB Guidelines 3/2019 on video devices (version 2.0, adopted 2020-01-29), paras 11-13: the GDPR household exemption is narrowly construed; following CJEU C-212/13 (Ryneš), constant recording that covers 'even partially, a public space' is not purely personal; a home camera on a fenced garden used only by the family can fall under the exemption 'provided that the video surveillance does not extend even partially to a public space or neighbouring property'.

EDPB Guidelines 3/2019 section 8: footage kept for a purpose such as detecting vandalism should 'be erased, ideally automatically, after a few days'; the longer the storage period (especially beyond 72 hours), the more argumentation is needed for its legitimacy.

labgrid (docs 'overview', repo HEAD b1b5b8e2 on 2026-11-11) is a Python board-control library with a pytest plugin for automated embedded testing; it models resources such as RawSerialPort, NetworkPowerPort and USB devices, and a coordinator plus exporters share remote boards across a lab.

METR (2025-07-10) randomized controlled trial: 16 experienced open-source developers on 246 real issues in their own large repositories took 19% longer with early-2025 AI tools than without; they expected a 24% speed-up and afterwards still believed AI had sped them up by 20%.
Chaos Mesh docs (repo HEAD 8e5a702e on 2026-11-11): PodChaos injects pod-failure, pod-kill and container-kill into Pods of any controller type via a Kubernetes custom resource applied with kubectl.

DigitalOcean custom-image limits (page last verified 2026-07-13): images must be under 100 GB uncompressed; UEFI boot is not supported (custom images must boot using BIOS); ISO and Windows images are not supported; no IPv6; networking via DHCP; an SSH key is required.

Spamhaus Policy Blocklist (PBL): a dataset of end-user IP ranges that 'should not be attempting to directly deliver unauthenticated SMTP email'; mail from those IPs is expected to go through an authenticated SMTP server of the ISP or an external mail service.

system76/firmware-open at 0cf80d89 ('System76 Open Firmware') pins coreboot @28fb508, edk2 @d2e0329 and System76's embedded-controller firmware ec @5f36175 as submodules: the laptop/desktop boot firmware and EC are built from open source.
